audience.name: Augusta-Richmond County civic and technology stakeholders

bridges.pageIntent: Reconnect proven civic-transparency work to a bounded modern Boundary First civic-engineering collaboration.

hero.title: We already proved that better representation can change how a city sees itself.
hero.support: CityWatch made projects, spending, infrastructure status, timelines, geography, and public-facing evidence more legible. Boundary First asks what the next generation of that civic representation should preserve, expose, and make repairable.

bridges.executiveBrief: The bridge is not a proposal to recreate an old portal. It is to use the CityWatch experience as proof of standing for a modern bounded civic instrument: choose one consequential public process, map the representations and responsibility chain around it, and build the smallest interface that makes status, consequence, evidence, and repair visible.

bridge.priorWork: CityWatch joined operational project information, public transparency, financial/accounting data, status, media, timeline, and map context into a citizen-facing representation.
bridge.currentMachinery: Boundary First adds explicit boundary, provenance, consequence, authority, contestability, and repair analysis around the represented system.
bridge.smallestUsefulNextStep: Select one bounded municipal process or infrastructure domain and produce a representation/consequence map plus a small public-facing prototype.

built: Requirements and delivery experience inside Augusta-Richmond County IT
proof.claimBoundary: Historical outcomes and awards should be linked to retained records or independent evidence before being used as public claims on the rendered page.

collaboration.ask: Choose one civic process where better representation would materially improve public understanding, operational coordination, or repair.

closing.primary: Start with one boundary the city already has to manage. Make it visible enough to act on.
